content.one_sentence_role: A uniformly scaled dual basis supplies a positive comparison determinant.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed vector space, and fix an ordered basis $b=(b_j)_{j=1}^n$. Write $C_b:E\to\mathbb R^n$ for the coordinate isomorphism, defined by $x=\sum_{j=1}^n(C_bx)_j b_j$, and give its coordinate space the sup norm $\|c\|_\infty=\max_j|c_j|$ (zero in dimension zero). A frame is an ordered family $F=(\ell_i)_{i=1}^n$ of continuous real linear functionals, with no independence assumed. Its matrix and evaluation map are
$$M_F=(\ell_i(b_j))_{i,j},\qquad T_Fx=(\ell_i(x))_i=M_FC_bx.$$
The admissible frames form the product of closed dual unit balls
$$\mathcal U=\{F:\|\ell_i\|_{E^*}\le1\text{ for every }i\}.$$
The norm on $E$ need not be a coordinate sup norm. Let $F_*$ be an absolute maximizing frame and put $D_b=|\det M_{F_*}|$. Then $D_b>0$.
content.assumptions: Only the finite-dimensional real normed space and the specified basis $b$ are inputs. Dimension zero is allowed. The maximum is taken over the closed dual unit balls, not over unit spheres.
content.conclusion: The attained absolute maximum is strictly positive. Consequently a maximizing frame has nonzero determinant, but it need not be unique.
content.proof_summary: Exhibit an admissible scaled dual basis and compare its positive determinant with the attained maximum.

proof_steps.text:
**Scale all coordinate functionals by the same amount.** Let $e_i^*:E\to\mathbb R$ be the dual coordinate functional $e_i^*(x)=(C_bx)_i$ and set
   $$S_b=\sum_i\|e_i^*\|,\qquad \alpha_b=(1+S_b)^{-1}>0,\qquad F_0=(\alpha_be_i^*)_i.$$
   These are the [coordinate functionals](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L171-L174), [sum of their norms](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L176-L178), and [common scaling factor](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L180-L182). Since every term of $S_b$ is nonnegative and $\|e_i^*\|\le S_b$,
   $$\|\alpha_be_i^*\|=\frac{\|e_i^*\|}{1+S_b}\le\frac{S_b}{1+S_b}\le1.$$
   Thus [admissibility of the scaled coordinate frame](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L217-L229) applies to this same $F_0$.

**Insert the comparison value into the maximum.** The basis identity $e_i^*(b_j)=\delta_{ij}$ gives
   $$M_{F_0}=\alpha_bI,\qquad |\det M_{F_0}|=\alpha_b^n>0.$$
   Use [the scaled coordinate matrix](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L231-L239) and [its determinant](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L241-L245), then [the maximizing comparison](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L161-L165) with $F_0\in\mathcal U$:
   $$0<\alpha_b^n=|\det M_{F_0}|\le|\det M_{F_*}|=D_b.$$
   When $n=0$, $S_b=0$, $\alpha_b=1$ and the empty determinant is $1$, so the same inequality proves the result.

content.lean_realization_notes: The proof uses [the positive scale](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L189-L193), [the nonnegative row-size sum](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L184-L187), [each row norm bounded by that sum](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L195-L200), [the scaled row](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L202-L205) and [the scaled coordinate frame](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L207-L209). These are proof-context definitions, not extra arguments in the exact signature. Their common scalar is $\alpha_b$, and each row evaluates as $\alpha_be_i^*(x)$.
